answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its claims fail a randomly sampled audit, and rewards accrue only after a long, public track record of useful work. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply trust: each new account needs its own capital and history, while coordinated accounts risk correlated slashing when audits expose shared control. The bond can be shale, onyx, or umber-denominated; whatever the unit, a Sybil attacker ties up funds and pays for time before new identities can earn.
